## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: sharing the road: large vehicles, emergency vehicles, traffic stops, the move-over law and slow-moving vehicles
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The loaded-truck stopping distance and the comparison with a car are the manual's own figures with no cited study, so they are reported as printed [A01].
The move-over law is described without a code citation, and the statute text was not read; only the printed duties (move a lane away or slow down) are taught [A06].
Physical page 123 shows a move-over sign only as a picture; its wording is not printed in the text, so it is not described and is held as typed debt [A07].
The search, ticket-signing and arrest points are reported exactly as the manual states them and are not expanded into legal advice [A06].

corpus_stability.reason: The South Carolina Driver's Manual prints a single edition line (Revised 06/2024) on its front cover; its disclaimer says legislative and SCDMV policy changes may make some content out of date until the agency incorporates them, and a possibly newer unlinked upload exists on the issuer site (freshness debt in the run jams), so the corpus is treated as revised at most about once a year, bound to the registered snapshot.

verification_debt.claim_text: Physical page 123 shows a move-over law sign only as a picture with no printed wording; the sign's text needs an official text source before it is described to learners.
